evidence: Lighthouse failed audit: button.owl-dot and button.owl-dot.active carousel controls do not have an accessible name.
user impact: Screen-reader users may not know the purpose or state of carousel controls.
recommended fix: Add accessible names to carousel dot buttons using meaningful aria-label values and ensure the active state is communicated.

evidence: Lighthouse failed audit: select elements were reported without associated label elements.
user impact: Screen-reader users may not know what information a select control requests.
recommended fix: Associate every select with a visible label using label-for/id or an equivalent accessible naming technique.

evidence: Lighthouse failed audit: one or more frame/iframe elements do not have a title attribute.
user impact: Screen-reader users may not understand the purpose of the embedded content.
recommended fix: Add a concise, descriptive title attribute to every iframe/frame and verify the title describes its content.

evidence: Lighthouse failed audit: multiple background/foreground color combinations have insufficient contrast.
user impact: Users with low vision or color-vision differences may have difficulty reading or distinguishing content.
recommended fix: Update foreground/background color combinations to meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements and retest with Lighthouse.

evidence: Lighthouse failed audit: heading elements are not in sequentially-descending order, indicating skipped heading levels.
user impact: Screen-reader users may have difficulty understanding page structure and navigating by headings.
recommended fix: Review the heading hierarchy and use logical h1-h2-h3 levels based on document structure rather than visual size.
